name: Machine Lateral Raise
summary: An isolation machine exercise that targets the lateral deltoids through guided shoulder abduction.

setup: Adjust the seat height so the machine's axis of rotation aligns with your shoulder joints.
Sit upright with your torso supported against the backrest or chest pad depending on machine design.
Place your elbows or forearms against the padded lever arms and grasp the handles lightly.
steps: Brace your core and initiate the movement by driving your elbows out and up away from your sides.
Raise the pads in a smooth arc until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top while maintaining tension in your side shoulders.
Lower the arms under control back to the starting position without letting the weight stack slam.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise your arms out to the sides; inhale as you slowly lower the weight.
cues: Keep shoulders depressed away from your ears

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders excessively at the top of the movement.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blades depressed and focus on driving outward rather than upward.

common_faults.fault: Using torso momentum or swinging to lift the weight.
common_faults.correction: Keep your back firmly against the pad and select a load that allows strict form.

common_faults.fault: Seat height misaligned with the machine pivot point.
common_faults.correction: Adjust the seat so your glenohumeral joints line up directly with the machine's rotational axis.

precautions: Do not force your arms above parallel if you experience impingement or shoulder pain.
